# arXiv Research

Search, read, cite, and analyze academic papers using the free arXiv API and Semantic Scholar API. No API keys, no dependencies — the bundled script uses only the Python stdlib.

## Quick Start: the `arxiv.py` script

Prefer `scripts/arxiv.py` over raw `curl` — it handles Atom XML parsing, versioned IDs, withdrawn-paper detection, and produces clean readable (or `--json`) output.

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Search papers | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "GRPO reinforcement learning" --max 10 --sort date` |
| Filtered search | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "attention" --author vaswani --category cs.CL` |
| Full metadata + abstract | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get 2601.02780,1706.03762` |
| BibTeX citation | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py bibtex 2601.02780` |
| Download PDF | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py download 2601.02780 --dest ./papers` |
| Latest in a category | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py new cs.CL --max 10` |
| Who cites this paper | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py cites 2601.02780 --max 20` |
| What this paper cites | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py similar 2601.02780` |
| Machine-readable output | append `--json` to any command |

Common flags: `--max N` (result count), `--sort relevance|date|updated`, `--start N` (pagination offset, search only), `--json`.

## Reading Paper Content

After finding a paper, read it with the `web_fetch` tool:

- Abstract page (fast, metadata + abstract): `https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780`
- Full paper as HTML (best for reading, when available): `https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02780`
- PDF: `https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.02780`

If HTML is unavailable and the PDF must be processed locally, `download` it first, then use a PDF-processing skill.

## Recommended Research Workflows

**Literature review on a topic**
1. `search "topic" --sort date --max 15` — recent work
2. `search "topic" --max 15` — seminal work (relevance-sorted)
3. Cross-check impact: `python3 /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get ID` then `cites ID --max 5` for citation counts
4. Read the top candidates via `web_fetch` on the abs/html URLs
5. `bibtex ID1,ID2,...` for the papers you keep

**Deep-dive a single paper**
1. `get ID` — full abstract, versions, journal ref, DOI
2. `refs ID` — what it builds on
3. `cites ID` — follow-up work (sorted by citation count)
4. `similar ID` — related papers you might have missed
5. Use `web_fetch` on the HTML/PDF for full text

**Stay current in a field**
- `new cs.AI --max 20` — latest submissions in a category
- Category taxonomy: https://arxiv.org/category_taxonomy — common ones: `cs.AI`, `cs.CL` (NLP), `cs.CV`, `cs.LG`, `cs.CR`, `stat.ML`, `math.OC`

## Raw API Reference (when the script isn't enough)

The script covers most needs; use the raw APIs for advanced queries.

### arXiv API (Atom XML)

```bash
curl -s "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:transformer&max_results=5"
```

Field prefixes: `all:` (everything), `ti:` (title), `au:` (author), `abs:` (abstract), `cat:` (category), `co:` (comment, e.g. `co:accepted+NeurIPS`).

Boolean syntax (URL-encode spaces as `+`):

```
all:GPT+OR+all:BERT              # OR
all:language+model+ANDNOT+all:vision   # AND NOT
ti:"chain+of+thought"            # exact phrase
au:hinton+AND+cat:cs.LG          # combined
```

Parameters: `sortBy` (`relevance`|`lastUpdatedDate`|`submittedDate`), `sortOrder`, `start`, `max_results`, `id_list` (comma-separated IDs).

### Semantic Scholar API (JSON)

arXiv has no citation data — Semantic Scholar fills that gap (free, ~1 req/sec unauthenticated).

```bash
# Paper details with citation counts
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/arXiv:2601.02780?fields=title,citationCount,influentialCitationCount,tldr"

# Author profile
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search?query=Yann+LeCun&fields=name,hIndex,citationCount,paperCount"

# Keyword search returning JSON (alternative to arXiv search)
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=GRPO&limit=5&fields=title,year,citationCount,externalIds"
```

Useful fields: `title`, `authors`, `year`, `abstract`, `tldr` (AI summary), `citationCount`, `influentialCitationCount`, `isOpenAccess`, `openAccessPdf`, `fieldsOfStudy`, `publicationVenue`, `externalIds` (arXiv ID, DOI).

## Important Details

**Rate limits** — arXiv: ~1 request / 3 seconds; Semantic Scholar: ~1 request / second. Space out consecutive calls; the script exits with a clear message on HTTP 429.

**ID formats** — new style `2402.03300`, old style `hep-th/0601001`. Both work everywhere.

**Versioning** — `arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780` resolves to the latest version; `...v2` is a specific immutable version. `bibtex` and `download` preserve the version suffix so citations match the content you actually read (later versions can change substantially).

**Withdrawn papers** — the script flags entries whose abstract indicates withdrawal/retraction with `[WITHDRAWN]`. Don't cite these without noting the status.

**Listings caveat** — `new CATEGORY` sorts by submission date via the search API; the official "new today" listing at `https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new` may group slightly differently (cross-lists, replacements).

</skill>

## Raw API Reference (when the script isn't enough)

The script covers most needs; use the raw APIs for advanced queries.

### arXiv API (Atom XML)

```bash
curl -s "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:transformer&max_results=5"
```

Field prefixes: `all:` (everything), `ti:` (title), `au:` (author), `abs:` (abstract), `cat:` (category), `co:` (comment, e.g. `co:accepted+NeurIPS`).

Boolean syntax (URL-encode spaces as `+`):

```
all:GPT+OR+all:BERT              # OR
all:language+model+ANDNOT+all:vision   # AND NOT
ti:"chain+of+thought"            # exact phrase
au:hinton+AND+cat:cs.LG          # combined
```

Parameters: `sortBy` (`relevance`|`lastUpdatedDate`|`submittedDate`), `sortOrder`, `start`, `max_results`, `id_list` (comma-separated IDs).

### Semantic Scholar API (JSON)

arXiv has no citation data — Semantic Scholar fills that gap (free, ~1 req/sec unauthenticated).

```bash
# Paper details with citation counts
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/arXiv:2601.02780?fields=title,citationCount,influentialCitationCount,tldr"

# Author profile
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search?query=Yann+LeCun&fields=name,hIndex,citationCount,paperCount"

# Keyword search returning JSON (alternative to arXiv search)
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=GRPO&limit=5&fields=title,year,citationCount,externalIds"
```

Useful fields: `title`, `authors`, `year`, `abstract`, `tldr` (AI summary), `citationCount`, `influentialCitationCount`, `isOpenAccess`, `openAccessPdf`, `fieldsOfStudy`, `publicationVenue`, `externalIds` (arXiv ID, DOI).

**Rate limits** — arXiv: ~1 request / 3 seconds; Semantic Scholar: ~1 request / second. Space out consecutive calls; the script exits with a clear message on HTTP 429.

**Versioning** — `arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780` resolves to the latest version; `...v2` is a specific immutable version. `bibtex` and `download` preserve the version suffix so citations match the content you actually read (later versions can change substantially).

result.content:
**Verdict: no blockers — the validator implements all four spec rules correctly for ASCII strings; only Unicode/boundary-definition edge cases remain (minor/nit).**

I read `auth.js` and probed it empirically with `node -e` (~30 cases: boundaries, non-strings, Unicode, repeated calls). Directory contains only `auth.js`; no test suite, as stated.

## Confirmed correct

- **All four rules, ASCII**: reject on 7 chars / empty / no-digit / no-uppercase / no-special; accept `"abcDEF1!"`, `"Aa1!aaaa"` etc. — all match spec. No logic inversion: each rule returns `false` on violation, falls through to `true` (`auth.js:7-19`).
- **Boundaries**: exactly 8 passes length, 7 fails (`auth.js:7`); empty string fails length; 8 whitespace-only spaces rejected (fails digit rule).
- **Non-strings**: `null`, `undefined`, numbers, booleans, objects, arrays, bigint all rejected by the `typeof` guard (`auth.js:4-6`). (`new String(...)` also rejected — acceptable, strings-that-must-be-primitives is the safe choice.)
- **No stateful regex**: all three regexes are literals with no flags — `flags in source: ['/[0-9]/','/[A-Z]/','/[^A-Za-z0-9]/']`, no `/g`/`/y`, so `lastIndex` can't cause alternating results. I verified by calling accept/reject inputs repeatedly: `true false true false`.

## Findings

1. **Minor — non-ASCII *letters* count as "special character"** (`auth.js:16`). `[^A-Za-z0-9]` matches any non-ASCII code unit, including letters. `"Aa1aaaaé"` and `"A1éééééé"` — zero punctuation/symbols — are **accepted**, violating rule (d) under any reasonable reading where "special character" means punctuation/symbol rather than "not an ASCII letter or digit". This is a false accept in a production signup flow: a letters+digits password can bypass the special-char requirement using an accented letter or emoji. Suggested fix: define special explicitly, e.g. test `/[\p{P}\p{S}]/u` (or an explicit symbol set) instead of `[^A-Za-z0-9]`.

2. **Minor — ASCII-only uppercase/digit checks cause false rejects** (`auth.js:13`, `auth.js:10`). `"ÀÀÀ1!ààà"` contains an uppercase letter (À), a digit, and a special character, yet is rejected because `/[A-Z]/` misses non-ASCII uppercase. Reading of "uppercase letter" as Unicode-aware is defensible, so this is a false reject rather than a security hole — but note the incoherence: accented letters *count* for the special rule but *don't count* for the uppercase rule. If the spec means ASCII, this is a nit; a Unicode-aware fix would use `\p{Lu}`/`\p{Nd}` with the `u` flag together with fix #1.

3. **Nit — length counted in UTF-16 code units, not characters** (`auth.js:7`). `"A1😀😀😀😀"` has 6 visible characters but `.length === 10`, so it passes the length rule. Astral characters count double. Fix by measuring with `[...password].length` (or `Array.from`) if "8 characters" means user-perceived characters.

4. **Nit — whitespace can serve as the "special character"** (`auth.js:16`). `"123456 A"` is accepted with a bare space as the only special char. Literally consistent (space is not alphanumeric) and the spec doesn't forbid it; note only if "special" is meant as visible punctuation. Fix #1 (`\p{P}\p{S}`) also excludes whitespace.

Untested area: this is a pure function with no I/O, so probing covered its full surface; nothing else in the directory to exercise.

# arXiv Research

Search, read, cite, and analyze academic papers using the free arXiv API and Semantic Scholar API. No API keys, no dependencies — the bundled script uses only the Python stdlib.

## Quick Start: the `arxiv.py` script

Prefer `scripts/arxiv.py` over raw `curl` — it handles Atom XML parsing, versioned IDs, withdrawn-paper detection, and produces clean readable (or `--json`) output.

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Search papers | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "GRPO reinforcement learning" --max 10 --sort date` |
| Filtered search | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "attention" --author vaswani --category cs.CL` |
| Full metadata + abstract | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get 2601.02780,1706.03762` |
| BibTeX citation | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py bibtex 2601.02780` |
| Download PDF | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py download 2601.02780 --dest ./papers` |
| Latest in a category | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py new cs.CL --max 10` |
| Who cites this paper | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py cites 2601.02780 --max 20` |
| What this paper cites | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py similar 2601.02780` |
| Machine-readable output | append `--json` to any command |

Common flags: `--max N` (result count), `--sort relevance|date|updated`, `--start N` (pagination offset, search only), `--json`.

## Reading Paper Content

After finding a paper, read it with the `web_fetch` tool:

- Abstract page (fast, metadata + abstract): `https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780`
- Full paper as HTML (best for reading, when available): `https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02780`
- PDF: `https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.02780`

If HTML is unavailable and the PDF must be processed locally, `download` it first, then use a PDF-processing skill.

## Recommended Research Workflows

**Literature review on a topic**
1. `search "topic" --sort date --max 15` — recent work
2. `search "topic" --max 15` — seminal work (relevance-sorted)
3. Cross-check impact: `python3 /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get ID` then `cites ID --max 5` for citation counts
4. Read the top candidates via `web_fetch` on the abs/html URLs
5. `bibtex ID1,ID2,...` for the papers you keep

**Deep-dive a single paper**
1. `get ID` — full abstract, versions, journal ref, DOI
2. `refs ID` — what it builds on
3. `cites ID` — follow-up work (sorted by citation count)
4. `similar ID` — related papers you might have missed
5. Use `web_fetch` on the HTML/PDF for full text

**Stay current in a field**
- `new cs.AI --max 20` — latest submissions in a category
- Category taxonomy: https://arxiv.org/category_taxonomy — common ones: `cs.AI`, `cs.CL` (NLP), `cs.CV`, `cs.LG`, `cs.CR`, `stat.ML`, `math.OC`

## Raw API Reference (when the script isn't enough)

The script covers most needs; use the raw APIs for advanced queries.

### arXiv API (Atom XML)

```bash
curl -s "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:transformer&max_results=5"
```

Field prefixes: `all:` (everything), `ti:` (title), `au:` (author), `abs:` (abstract), `cat:` (category), `co:` (comment, e.g. `co:accepted+NeurIPS`).

Boolean syntax (URL-encode spaces as `+`):

```
all:GPT+OR+all:BERT              # OR
all:language+model+ANDNOT+all:vision   # AND NOT
ti:"chain+of+thought"            # exact phrase
au:hinton+AND+cat:cs.LG          # combined
```

Parameters: `sortBy` (`relevance`|`lastUpdatedDate`|`submittedDate`), `sortOrder`, `start`, `max_results`, `id_list` (comma-separated IDs).

### Semantic Scholar API (JSON)

arXiv has no citation data — Semantic Scholar fills that gap (free, ~1 req/sec unauthenticated).

```bash
# Paper details with citation counts
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/arXiv:2601.02780?fields=title,citationCount,influentialCitationCount,tldr"

# Author profile
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search?query=Yann+LeCun&fields=name,hIndex,citationCount,paperCount"

# Keyword search returning JSON (alternative to arXiv search)
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=GRPO&limit=5&fields=title,year,citationCount,externalIds"
```

Useful fields: `title`, `authors`, `year`, `abstract`, `tldr` (AI summary), `citationCount`, `influentialCitationCount`, `isOpenAccess`, `openAccessPdf`, `fieldsOfStudy`, `publicationVenue`, `externalIds` (arXiv ID, DOI).

## Important Details

**Rate limits** — arXiv: ~1 request / 3 seconds; Semantic Scholar: ~1 request / second. Space out consecutive calls; the script exits with a clear message on HTTP 429.

**ID formats** — new style `2402.03300`, old style `hep-th/0601001`. Both work everywhere.

**Versioning** — `arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780` resolves to the latest version; `...v2` is a specific immutable version. `bibtex` and `download` preserve the version suffix so citations match the content you actually read (later versions can change substantially).

**Withdrawn papers** — the script flags entries whose abstract indicates withdrawal/retraction with `[WITHDRAWN]`. Don't cite these without noting the status.

**Listings caveat** — `new CATEGORY` sorts by submission date via the search API; the official "new today" listing at `https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new` may group slightly differently (cross-lists, replacements).

</skill>

# arXiv Research

Search, read, cite, and analyze academic papers using the free arXiv API and Semantic Scholar API. No API keys, no dependencies — the bundled script uses only the Python stdlib.

## Quick Start: the `arxiv.py` script

Prefer `scripts/arxiv.py` over raw `curl` — it handles Atom XML parsing, versioned IDs, withdrawn-paper detection, and produces clean readable (or `--json`) output.

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Search papers | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "GRPO reinforcement learning" --max 10 --sort date` |
| Filtered search | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py search "attention" --author vaswani --category cs.CL` |
| Full metadata + abstract | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get 2601.02780,1706.03762` |
| BibTeX citation | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py bibtex 2601.02780` |
| Download PDF | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py download 2601.02780 --dest ./papers` |
| Latest in a category | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py new cs.CL --max 10` |
| Who cites this paper | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py cites 2601.02780 --max 20` |
| What this paper cites | `python /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py similar 2601.02780` |
| Machine-readable output | append `--json` to any command |

Common flags: `--max N` (result count), `--sort relevance|date|updated`, `--start N` (pagination offset, search only), `--json`.

## Reading Paper Content

After finding a paper, read it with the `web_fetch` tool:

- Abstract page (fast, metadata + abstract): `https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780`
- Full paper as HTML (best for reading, when available): `https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02780`
- PDF: `https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.02780`

If HTML is unavailable and the PDF must be processed locally, `download` it first, then use a PDF-processing skill.

## Recommended Research Workflows

**Literature review on a topic**
1. `search "topic" --sort date --max 15` — recent work
2. `search "topic" --max 15` — seminal work (relevance-sorted)
3. Cross-check impact: `python3 /home/ubuntu/pet/cast/prompts/skills/arxiv/scripts/arxiv.py get ID` then `cites ID --max 5` for citation counts
4. Read the top candidates via `web_fetch` on the abs/html URLs
5. `bibtex ID1,ID2,...` for the papers you keep

**Deep-dive a single paper**
1. `get ID` — full abstract, versions, journal ref, DOI
2. `refs ID` — what it builds on
3. `cites ID` — follow-up work (sorted by citation count)
4. `similar ID` — related papers you might have missed
5. Use `web_fetch` on the HTML/PDF for full text

**Stay current in a field**
- `new cs.AI --max 20` — latest submissions in a category
- Category taxonomy: https://arxiv.org/category_taxonomy — common ones: `cs.AI`, `cs.CL` (NLP), `cs.CV`, `cs.LG`, `cs.CR`, `stat.ML`, `math.OC`

## Raw API Reference (when the script isn't enough)

The script covers most needs; use the raw APIs for advanced queries.

### arXiv API (Atom XML)

```bash
curl -s "https://export.arxiv.org/api/query?search_query=all:transformer&max_results=5"
```

Field prefixes: `all:` (everything), `ti:` (title), `au:` (author), `abs:` (abstract), `cat:` (category), `co:` (comment, e.g. `co:accepted+NeurIPS`).

Boolean syntax (URL-encode spaces as `+`):

```
all:GPT+OR+all:BERT              # OR
all:language+model+ANDNOT+all:vision   # AND NOT
ti:"chain+of+thought"            # exact phrase
au:hinton+AND+cat:cs.LG          # combined
```

Parameters: `sortBy` (`relevance`|`lastUpdatedDate`|`submittedDate`), `sortOrder`, `start`, `max_results`, `id_list` (comma-separated IDs).

### Semantic Scholar API (JSON)

arXiv has no citation data — Semantic Scholar fills that gap (free, ~1 req/sec unauthenticated).

```bash
# Paper details with citation counts
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/arXiv:2601.02780?fields=title,citationCount,influentialCitationCount,tldr"

# Author profile
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/author/search?query=Yann+LeCun&fields=name,hIndex,citationCount,paperCount"

# Keyword search returning JSON (alternative to arXiv search)
curl -s "https://api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/search?query=GRPO&limit=5&fields=title,year,citationCount,externalIds"
```

Useful fields: `title`, `authors`, `year`, `abstract`, `tldr` (AI summary), `citationCount`, `influentialCitationCount`, `isOpenAccess`, `openAccessPdf`, `fieldsOfStudy`, `publicationVenue`, `externalIds` (arXiv ID, DOI).

## Important Details

**Rate limits** — arXiv: ~1 request / 3 seconds; Semantic Scholar: ~1 request / second. Space out consecutive calls; the script exits with a clear message on HTTP 429.

**ID formats** — new style `2402.03300`, old style `hep-th/0601001`. Both work everywhere.

**Versioning** — `arxiv.org/abs/2601.02780` resolves to the latest version; `...v2` is a specific immutable version. `bibtex` and `download` preserve the version suffix so citations match the content you actually read (later versions can change substantially).

**Withdrawn papers** — the script flags entries whose abstract indicates withdrawal/retraction with `[WITHDRAWN]`. Don't cite these without noting the status.

**Listings caveat** — `new CATEGORY` sorts by submission date via the search API; the official "new today" listing at `https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new` may group slightly differently (cross-lists, replacements).

result.content:
## Verdict: implementation meets the stated requirements — no correctness bugs found. Remaining items are design/edge-case caveats worth deciding on, not defects.

I read `auth.js` (13 lines) and ran 24 empirical cases against the real module via `require`, plus a 5M-character timing probe.

### Correctness vs. requirements — confirmed correct

- **Length boundary (auth.js:6)** — `password.length >= 8` rejects 7 chars and accepts exactly 8 (`"Ab1!xyzw"` → `true`, `"Ab1!xyz"` → `false`). Matches "under 8 characters" being rejected.
- **Regex checks (auth.js:7-9)** — each is a presence check via `.test()`, and all four requirements are AND-ed with positive presence tests, so there is **no logic inversion** (verified: each single-class-missing variant is rejected).
- **Missing anchors are NOT a bug here.** The assignment asks whether absent anchors change behavior for a single match check — they don't. `RegExp.prototype.test` returns true if the pattern matches *anywhere*, which is exactly the semantics wanted for "contains a digit/uppercase/special". Adding `^...$` would actually break the checks (e.g. `/^[0-9]$/` would only match a one-digit string). Anchors matter for format checks ("entire string is digits"), not presence checks.
- **ReDoS (auth.js:7-9)** — none. All three patterns are single character classes with no quantifiers, nesting, or alternation; matching is O(n). A 5M-character input was processed in ~9ms.
- **Empty string** — rejected by the length check. Verified.

### Findings (all low severity / design decisions)

**1. "Special character" is defined as "any non-ASCII-alphanumeric" (auth.js:9) — broader than the usual meaning.**
`/[^A-Za-z0-9]/` treats *everything* outside ASCII letters/digits as special, including:
- whitespace and control characters (`"Abc1 defg"`, `"Abc1\ndefg"` both pass),
- emoji and lone surrogates,
- and, most surprisingly, **Unicode letters**: `"Abc1défg"` passes with no conventional symbol at all, because `é`/`ß`/Cyrillic letters fall outside `A-Za-z`. Same for Unicode digits (`١`, `１`) — they don't satisfy the digit check (ASCII-only `[0-9]`, which is at least internally consistent) but they do satisfy the "special" check.

If the intent is "contains a symbol like `!@#$`", this accepts passwords the policy was meant to reject. If the intent is literally "not alphanumeric ASCII", it's correct as written. The stated requirement doesn't define "special character", so this is a policy ambiguity to confirm, not a code bug. Suggested fix: decide the definition explicitly — e.g. restrict to a punctuation class, or keep the broad class but explicitly exclude whitespace/control chars.

**2. Length counts UTF-16 code units, not user-perceived characters (auth.js:6).**
A 7-grapheme password `"😀😀😀😀P1!"` passes (11 code units). Conversely a combining-mark sequence inflates length without adding visible characters. If "8 characters" means 8 graphemes, use `Intl.Segmenter` or `Array.from(password).length`; if 8 UTF-16 units is acceptable (common practice), no change needed. Verified both directions empirically.

**3. Non-string inputs are silently rejected (auth.js:2-4).**
`null`, `undefined`, numbers, plain objects, arrays, and `new String("...")` all return `false` with no error. This is safe for a signup flow (no crash, no coercion — notably `String(obj)` coercion attacks are impossible). The only risk: a caller bug passing `undefined` is masked as "invalid password" rather than surfacing. Acceptable default; alternatively throw `TypeError` for non-strings if you want programmer errors to be loud.

**4. No maximum length (auth.js:6).**
A 1MB password is accepted. The validator itself handles it in linear time, but downstream password hashing cost/memory (and bcrypt's 72-byte truncation, if used) makes an upper bound (commonly 128–256 chars) good practice for a production signup flow. Not a stated requirement.

### Explicitly fine
- No global-flag `lastIndex` statefulness (none of the regexes use `/g`).
- No cache-able state, no module-level mutable state — the function is pure and safe to reuse across requests.
- `module.exports = { validatePassword }` (auth.js:13) is straightforward.

### Bottom line
The implementation satisfies all four stated requirements exactly (verified at the 8-char boundary and for each missing character class), has no ReDoS or logic-inversion issues, and handles non-string/empty input safely. The open questions are policy-level: what counts as a "special character" (Unicode letters/whitespace currently qualify), whether length should count graphemes, and whether to cap maximum length.
